name: East Village
vibe: Tenement blocks, dive bars and the loudest cheap dinner in Manhattan — St Marks never quite grew up

name: West Village
vibe: The one part of the grid that isn't one — crooked leafy streets, stoops, and rents to match

name: Lower East Side
vibe: Where every wave of arrivals landed first, now the bars that stay open latest

name: Chelsea
vibe: Gallery district under the High Line — art on the ground floor, the river two blocks west

name: Upper West Side
vibe: Lincoln Center, the park on both sides, and pre-war apartments full of people who never left

name: Harlem
vibe: Brownstone rows, the Apollo, Sunday gospel and the best-value space left on the island

name: Washington Heights
vibe: Dominican uptown on the high ground — the Cloisters, Fort Tryon, and Manhattan you can afford

name: Williamsburg
vibe: The waterfront with the skyline in front of it — the L to Manhattan, Smorgasburg on Saturdays

name: Greenpoint
vibe: Little Poland on the creek — pierogi, the G train, and the quietest corner of north Brooklyn

name: Bushwick
vibe: Painted warehouse walls, late venues and studio space — where the art moved when Williamsburg priced out

name: Bedford-Stuyvesant
vibe: The deepest brownstone streets in the city, block after block, with the stoop life to go with them

name: Park Slope
vibe: Prospect Park at the end of the street, farmers' market on Saturday — Brooklyn's family answer

name: Astoria
vibe: Greek tavernas, Egyptian cafés and a Czech beer garden — twenty minutes from Midtown, half the rent

name: Long Island City
vibe: New towers looking straight back at Manhattan, MoMA PS1, and one stop under the river

name: Jackson Heights
vibe: The most-spoken-languages few blocks on earth — momos, arepas and Little India on 74th

name: Flushing
vibe: The city's real Chinatown plus Korean Northern Boulevard — the 7 train's last and best stop

name: Mott Haven
vibe: The South Bronx where hip-hop started — waterfront studios, and the cheapest way into the city

name: Rockaway Beach
vibe: Surf and boardwalk at the end of the A train — the only city beach you reach on a MetroCard

name: Beacon
vibe: Ninety minutes up the Hudson on Metro-North — Dia:Beacon, Main Street, and Breakneck Ridge to climb
